summary: Iter 82 reassessment-prompt grace-period fix verified. All 5 pytest tests in tests/test_iter82_reassess_grace_period.py PASS. HTTP-level verification confirms GET /api/reassessment/prompts returns {"prompts": []} for a brand-new signup, while existing seeded client (client@crewfit.com, with historical completions) still receives 2 prompts as expected per PR note. Frontend UI verification: fresh signup routes to /assessment gate (not /home) — providing an additional layer of protection. No 'MISSED SESSIONS', 'CREWFIT INTELLIGENCE', 'QUICK CHECK-IN', 'Take 90s', or 'Roster confirmed' text appears anywhere in rendered page content for the fresh user. Two-layer defence in server.py (_emit_reassessment_prompt guard + endpoint filter) confirmed working.
critical_code_review_comments: Guard implementation in _emit_reassessment_prompt (server.py ~2248) correctly parses ISO created_at (handles Z suffix + tz-naive), computes age in days, and only suppresses when age<3 AND completed_workouts==0. Exception handler is broad (bare except) which is acceptable for a defensive guard.

Endpoint filter in /api/reassessment/prompts (server.py ~2285) applies two conditions: (a) fresh account + 0 completions -> return [] regardless of DB, and (b) any user with 0 completions -> strip missed_workouts kind. Order and logic are correct.
Existing seed client with historical completions correctly still receives prompts (2 in verification), matching PR expectation.
seed_data_creation: Created 2 throwaway fresh signup users (uifr_* and uilog_*@test.com) during verification. Users left in DB but do not affect any flow — grace period logic handles them correctly.

rca_of_issue: Original bug: brand-new users saw 'MISSED SESSIONS · CHECK-IN' + 'CREWFIT INTELLIGENCE · Roster confirmed' cards on first login. Root cause: (1) _emit_reassessment_prompt had no account-age guard, so any legacy/seeded prompt row could survive; (2) GET /api/reassessment/prompts returned all undismissed rows without checking whether the user had actually completed any workouts. Fix: two-layer defence — emit-side guard (age<3d AND completed==0 -> no-op) and read-side guard (fresh account -> return []; also universally strip missed_workouts when completed==0). Verification: pytest 5/5 green + HTTP fresh-signup returns [] + UI shows no nag strings.
